1|--- 2|name: google-workspace 3|description: "Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets via gws CLI or Python." 4|version: 1.2.0 5|author: Nous Research 6|license: MIT 7|platforms: [linux, macos, windows] 8|required_credential_files: 9| - path: google_token.json 10| description: Google OAuth2 token (created by setup script) 11| - path: google_client_secret.json 12| description: Google OAuth2 client credentials (downloaded from Google Cloud Console) 13|metadata: 14| hermes: 15| tags: [Google, Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Sheets, Docs, Contacts, Email, OAuth] 16| homepage: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent 17| related_skills: [himalaya] 18|--- 19| 20|# Google Workspace 21| 22|Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Contacts, Sheets, and Docs — through Hermes-managed OAuth and a thin CLI wrapper. When `gws` is installed, the skill uses it as the execution backend for broader Google Workspace coverage; otherwise it falls back to the bundled Python client implementation. 23| 24|## References 25| 26|- `references/gmail-search-syntax.md` — Gmail search operators (is:unread, from:, newer_than:, etc.) 27|- `references/daily-brief.md` — daily/morning brief procedure: schedule + conflicts + meeting prep + urgent mail from Gmail and Calendar. Load it when the user asks for a morning brief, meeting preparation, or "what's on my calendar and what email needs attention." 28| 29|## Scripts 30| 31|- `scripts/setup.py` — OAuth2 setup (run once to authorize) 32|- `scripts/google_api.py` — compatibility wrapper CLI. It prefers `gws` for operations when available, while preserving Hermes' existing JSON output contract. 33| 34|## First-Time Setup 35| 36|The setup is fully non-interactive — you drive it step by step so it works 37|on CLI, Telegram, Discord, or any platform. 38| 39|Run the setup script with Python from the Hermes environment, not an unrelated 40|system Python. `--install-deps` syncs Hermes' declared Google extra through PM; 41|after syncing, restart Hermes and rerun the OAuth command. If Hermes is not 42|importable, use `hermes setup` first rather than installing packages with pip. 43| 44|Define a shorthand first: 45| 46|```bash 47|GSETUP="python ${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/productivity/google-workspace/scripts/setup.py" 48|``` 49| 50|### Step 0: Check if already set up 51| 52|```bash 53|$GSETUP --check 54|``` 55| 56|If it prints `AUTHENTICATED`, skip to Usage — setup is already done. 57| 58|### Step 1: Triage — ask the user what they need 59| 60|Before starting OAuth setup, ask the user TWO questions: 61| 62|**Question 1: "What Google services do you need? Just email, or also 63|Calendar/Drive/Sheets/Docs?"** 64| 65|- **Email only** → They don't need this skill at all. Use the `himalaya` skill 66| instead — it works with a Gmail App Password (Settings → Security → App 67| Passwords) and takes 2 minutes to set up. No Google Cloud project needed. 68| Load the himalaya skill and follow its setup instructions. 69| 70|- **Email + Calendar** → Continue with this skill, but use 71| `--services email,calendar` during auth so the consent screen only asks for 72| the scopes they actually need. 73| 74|- **Calendar/Drive/Sheets/Docs only** → Continue with this skill and use a 75| narrower `--services` set like `calendar,drive,sheets,docs`. 76| 77|- **Full Workspace access** → Continue with this skill and use the default 78| `all` service set. 79| 80|**Question 2: "Does your Google account use Advanced Protection (hardware 81|security keys required to sign in)? If you're not sure, you probably don't 82|— it's something you would have explicitly enrolled in."** 83| 84|- **No / Not sure** → Normal setup. Continue below. 85|- **Yes** → Their Workspace admin must add the OAuth client ID to the org's 86| allowed apps list before Step 4 will work. Let them know upfront. 87| 88|### Step 2: Create OAuth credentials (one-time, ~5 minutes) 89| 90|Tell the user: 91| 92|> You need a Google Cloud OAuth client. This is a one-time setup: 93|> 94|> 1. Create or select a project: 95|> https://console.cloud.google.com/projectselector2/home/dashboard 96|> 2. Enable the required APIs from the API Library: 97|> https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library 98|> Enable: Gmail API, Google Calendar API, Google Drive API, 99|> Google Sheets API, Google Docs API, People API 100|> 3. Create the OAuth client here: 101|> https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials 102|> Credentials → Create Credentials → OAuth 2.0 Client ID 103|> 4. Application type: "Desktop app" → Create 104|> 5. If the app is still in Testing, add the user's Google account as a test user here: 105|> https://console.cloud.google.com/auth/audience 106|> Audience → Test users → Add users 107|> 6. Download the JSON file and tell me the file path 108|> 109|> Important Hermes CLI note: if the file path starts with `/`, do NOT send only the bare path as its own message in the CLI, because it can be mistaken for a slash command. Send it in a sentence instead, like: 110|> `The JSON file path is: ~/Downloads/client_secret_....json` 111| 112|Once they provide the path: 113| 114|```bash 115|$GSETUP --client-secret /path/to/client_secret.json 116|``` 117| 118|If they paste the raw client ID / client secret values instead of a file path, 119|write a valid Desktop OAuth JSON file for them yourself, save it somewhere 120|explicit (for example `~/Downloads/hermes-google-client-secret.json`), then run 121|`--client-secret` against that file. 122| 123|### Step 3: Get authorization URL 124| 125|Use the service set chosen in Step 1. Examples: 126| 127|```bash 128|$GSETUP --auth-url --services email,calendar --format json 129|$GSETUP --auth-url --services calendar,drive,sheets,docs --format json 130|$GSETUP --auth-url --services all --format json 131|``` 132| 133|This returns JSON with an `auth_url` field and also saves the exact URL to 134|`~/.hermes/google_oauth_last_url.txt`. 135| 136|Agent rules for this step: 137|- Extract the `auth_url` field and send that exact URL to the user as a single line. 138|- Tell the user that the browser will likely fail on `http://localhost:1` after approval, and that this is expected. 139|- Tell them to copy the ENTIRE redirected URL from the browser address bar. 140|- If the user gets `Error 403: access_denied`, send them directly to `https://console.cloud.google.com/auth/audience` to add themselves as a test user. 141| 142|### Step 4: Exchange the code 143| 144|The user will paste back either a URL like `http://localhost:1/?code=4/0A...&scope=...` 145|or just the code string. Either works. The `--auth-url` step stores a temporary 146|pending OAuth session locally so `--auth-code` can complete the PKCE exchange 147|later, even on headless systems: 148| 149|```bash 150|$GSETUP --auth-code "THE_URL_OR_CODE_THE_USER_PASTED" --format json 151|``` 152| 153|If `--auth-code` fails because the code expired, was already used, or came from 154|an older browser tab, it now returns a fresh `fresh_auth_url`. In that case, 155|immediately send the new URL to the user and have them retry with the newest 156|browser redirect only. 157| 158|### Step 5: Verify 159| 160|```bash 161|$GSETUP --check 162|``` 163| 164|Should print `AUTHENTICATED`. Setup is complete — token refreshes automatically from now on. 165| 166|### Notes 167| 168|- Token is stored at `~/.hermes/google_token.json` and auto-refreshes. 169|- Pending OAuth session state/verifier are stored temporarily at `~/.hermes/google_oauth_pending.json` until exchange completes. 170|- If `gws` is installed, `google_api.py` points it at the same `~/.hermes/google_token.json` credentials file. Users do not need to run a separate `gws auth login` flow. 171|- To revoke: `$GSETUP --revoke` 172| 173|## Usage 174| 175|All commands go through the API script. Set `GAPI` as a shorthand: 176| 177|```bash 178|GAPI="python ${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/productivity/google-workspace/scripts/google_api.py" 179|``` 180| 181|### Gmail 182| 183|```bash 184|# Search (returns JSON array with id, from, subject, date, snippet) 185|$GAPI gmail search "is:unread" --max 10 186|$GAPI gmail search "from:boss@company.com newer_than:1d" 187|$GAPI gmail search "has:attachment filename:pdf newer_than:7d" 188| 189|# Read full message (returns JSON with body text) 190|$GAPI gmail get MESSAGE_ID 191| 192|# Send 193|$GAPI gmail send --to user@example.com --subject "Hello" --body "Message text" 194|$GAPI gmail send --to user@example.com --subject "Report" --body "

Q4

Details...

" --html 195|$GAPI gmail send --to user@example.com --subject "Hello" --from '"Research Agent" ' --body "Message text" 196| 197|# Reply (automatically threads and sets In-Reply-To) 198|$GAPI gmail reply MESSAGE_ID --body "Thanks, that works for me." 199|$GAPI gmail reply MESSAGE_ID --from '"Support Bot" ' --body "Thanks" 200| 201|# Labels 202|$GAPI gmail labels 203|$GAPI gmail modify MESSAGE_ID --add-labels LABEL_ID 204|$GAPI gmail modify MESSAGE_ID --remove-labels UNREAD 205|``` 206| 207|### Calendar 208| 209|```bash 210|# List events (defaults to next 7 days) 211|$GAPI calendar list 212|$GAPI calendar list --start 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z --end 2026-03-07T23:59:59Z 213| 214|# Create event (ISO 8601 with timezone required) 215|$GAPI calendar create --summary "Team Standup" --start 2026-03-01T10:00:00-06:00 --end 2026-03-01T10:30:00-06:00 216|$GAPI calendar create --summary "Lunch" --start 2026-03-01T12:00:00Z --end 2026-03-01T13:00:00Z --location "Cafe" 217|$GAPI calendar create --summary "Review" --start 2026-03-01T14:00:00Z --end 2026-03-01T15:00:00Z --attendees "alice@co.com,bob@co.com" 218| 219|# Delete event 220|$GAPI calendar delete EVENT_ID 221|``` 222| 223|### Drive 224| 225|```bash 226|# Search existing files 227|$GAPI drive search "quarterly report" --max 10 228|$GAPI drive search "mimeType='application/pdf'" --raw-query --max 5 229| 230|# Get metadata for a single file 231|$GAPI drive get FILE_ID 232| 233|# Upload a local file (auto-detects MIME type) 234|$GAPI drive upload /path/to/report.pdf 235|$GAPI drive upload /path/to/image.png --name "Logo.png" --parent FOLDER_ID 236| 237|# Download (binary files download as-is; Google-native files export to a 238|# sensible default — Docs→pdf, Sheets→csv, Slides→pdf, Drawings→png) 239|$GAPI drive download FILE_ID 240|$GAPI drive download DOC_ID --output ~/doc.pdf 241|$GAPI drive download DOC_ID --export-mime text/plain --output ~/doc.txt 242| 243|# Create a folder 244|$GAPI drive create-folder "Reports" 245|$GAPI drive create-folder "Q4" --parent FOLDER_ID 246| 247|# Share 248|$GAPI drive share FILE_ID --email alice@example.com --role reader 249|$GAPI drive share FILE_ID --email alice@example.com --role writer --notify 250|$GAPI drive share FILE_ID --type anyone --role reader # anyone with link 251|$GAPI drive share FILE_ID --type domain --domain example.com --role reader 252| 253|# Delete — defaults to trash (reversible). Use --permanent to skip the trash. 254|$GAPI drive delete FILE_ID 255|$GAPI drive delete FILE_ID --permanent 256|``` 257| 258|### Contacts 259| 260|```bash 261|$GAPI contacts list --max 20 262|``` 263| 264|### Sheets 265| 266|```bash 267|# Create a new spreadsheet 268|$GAPI sheets create --title "Q4 Budget" 269|$GAPI sheets create --title "Inventory" --sheet-name "Stock" 270| 271|# Read 272|$GAPI sheets get SHEET_ID "Sheet1!A1:D10" 273| 274|# Write 275|$GAPI sheets update SHEET_ID "Sheet1!A1:B2" --values '[["Name","Score"],["Alice","95"]]' 276| 277|# Append rows 278|$GAPI sheets append SHEET_ID "Sheet1!A:C" --values '[["new","row","data"]]' 279|``` 280| 281|### Docs 282| 283|```bash 284|# Read (a tabbed Doc returns a "tabs" array; single-tab and legacy Docs also return "body") 285|$GAPI docs get DOC_ID 286|$GAPI docs get DOC_ID --tab TAB_ID # read one tab of a tabbed Doc 287| 288|# Create a new Doc (optionally seeded with body text) 289|$GAPI docs create --title "Meeting Notes" 290|$GAPI docs create --title "Draft" --body "First paragraph..." 291| 292|# Append text to the end of an existing Doc 293|$GAPI docs append DOC_ID --text "Additional content to append" 294|$GAPI docs append DOC_ID --tab TAB_ID --text "..." # --tab required when the Doc has multiple tabs 295|``` 296| 297|## Output Format 298| 299|All commands return JSON. Parse with `jq` or read directly. Key fields: 300| 301|- **Gmail search**: `[{id, threadId, from, to, subject, date, snippet, labels}]` 302|- **Gmail get**: `{id, threadId, from, to, subject, date, labels, body}` 303|- **Gmail send/reply**: `{status: "sent", id, threadId}` 304|- **Calendar list**: `[{id, summary, start, end, location, description, htmlLink}]` 305|- **Calendar create**: `{status: "created", id, summary, htmlLink}` 306|- **Drive search**: `[{id, name, mimeType, modifiedTime, webViewLink}]` 307|- **Drive get**: `{id, name, mimeType, modifiedTime, size, webViewLink, parents, owners}` 308|- **Drive upload**: `{status: "uploaded", id, name, mimeType, webViewLink}` 309|- **Drive download**: `{status: "downloaded", id, name, path, mimeType}` 310|- **Drive create-folder**: `{status: "created", id, name, webViewLink}` 311|- **Drive share**: `{status: "shared", permissionId, fileId, role, type}` 312|- **Drive delete**: `{status: "trashed" | "deleted", fileId, permanent}` 313|- **Contacts list**: `[{name, emails: [...], phones: [...]}]` 314|- **Sheets get**: `[[cell, cell, ...], ...]` 315|- **Sheets create**: `{status: "created", spreadsheetId, title, spreadsheetUrl}` 316|- **Docs create**: `{status: "created", documentId, title, url}` 317|- **Docs append**: `{status: "appended", documentId, inserted_at, characters}` 318| 319|## Rules 320| 321|1. **Never send email, create/delete calendar events, delete Drive files, share files, or modify Docs/Sheets without confirming with the user first.** Show what will be done (recipients, file IDs, content, share role) and ask for approval. For `drive delete`, prefer the default trash (reversible) over `--permanent`. 322|2. **Check auth before first use** — run `setup.py --check`. If it fails, guide the user through setup. 323|3. **Use the Gmail search syntax reference** for complex queries — load it with `skill_view("google-workspace", file_path="references/gmail-search-syntax.md")`. 324|4. **Calendar times must include timezone** — always use ISO 8601 with offset (e.g., `2026-03-01T10:00:00-06:00`) or UTC (`Z`). 325|5. **Respect rate limits** — avoid rapid-fire sequential API calls. Batch reads when possible. 326| 327|## Troubleshooting 328| 329|| Problem | Fix | 330||---------|-----| 331|| `NOT_AUTHENTICATED` | Run setup Steps 2-5 above | 332|| `REFRESH_FAILED` | Token revoked or expired — redo Steps 3-5 | 333|| `HttpError 403: Insufficient Permission` | Missing API scope — `$GSETUP --revoke` then redo Steps 3-5 | 334|| `AUTHENTICATED (partial)` or "Token missing scopes" | New write capabilities (Drive write/delete, Docs create/edit) require re-authorization. `$GSETUP --revoke` then redo Steps 3-5 to grant the upgraded scopes. | 335|| `HttpError 403: Access Not Configured` | API not enabled — user needs to enable it in Google Cloud Console | 336|| `ModuleNotFoundError` | Run `$GSETUP --install-deps` | 337|| Advanced Protection blocks auth | Workspace admin must allowlist the OAuth client ID | 338| 339|## Revoking Access 340| 341|```bash 342|$GSETUP --revoke 343|``` 344|
